newsitem.title: USA: Judge extends time for computer injury claims.
newsitem.headline: Judge extends time for computer injury claims.

text.p: A federal judge has extended the amount of time that plaintiffs can sue computer manufacturers for repetitive stress injuries they allege are caused by typing on keyboards.

U.S. District Judge Jack Weinstein of Brooklyn, N.Y., in a decision issued last week, ruled that the three-year statute of limitation for filing a claim begins running when the plaintiff suffers pain and symptoms of an injury.

He said that a New York state court was wrong when it ruled last month that the statute begins to run when the plaintiff first began to use the keyboard, even if the pain does not occur for many years.
Weinstein said that the Appellate Division, First Division's application of the statute was not an accurate statement of New York State law.

The federal judge made his ruling in a case brought against Apple Computers, Inc. by a woman who began using computer keyboards in 1988. She did not begin to feel pain until 1993 and filed suit 13 months later.
